summary: The post-midterm landscape is reshaping UAP disclosure politics in ways that cut against initial expectations. Key disclosure advocates retained their seats in Congress, preserving momentum for legislative action even as Democrats lost the House majority, while Trump signaled renewed interest in the issue by publicly stating that Air Force pilots have reported strange sightings to him. The Pentagon's Anomaly Office remains under scrutiny following new revelations about black triangular objects and FBI deployments, though the bureau declined to explain specific operational details. With control of disclosure strategy potentially shifting back to the executive branch, observers are watching whether Trump will follow through on converting public interest into binding legislation rather than relying on administrative action alone. The week also saw a batch of archived UAP documents from 2021 and 2022 added to the public record, adding texture to the historical record even as current policy debates intensify.
